text: Active geo-replication is Azure SQL Database's built-in DR feature — a continuously-updated, readable secondary in a different Azure region. This is the mechanism that gets you out of the region entirely.

Geo-replication is always asynchronous — no synchronous option across regions. That means a realistic RPO of seconds to low minutes, not zero. A true zero-data-loss cross-region requirement can't be met by geo-replication alone.

A database can have up to four geo-replicated secondaries, each fully readable at all times — useful for disaster recovery, offloading reporting workloads, or giving distant users a low-latency read copy.

This is what it looks like configured — the Azure Portal showing the primary database, its secondary in another region, and the replication link between them. One primary, one or more independently readable secondaries.
Promoting a secondary today is a manual, explicit failover. Next up: Azure SQL Failover Groups — the layer above geo-replication that also manages the connection endpoint.
